items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: We were the first mixed band... Cannonball gave me his card. So my dad had a street dance. So he said, 'Hire him for the gig.'

ctx.x: And you had an encounter that’s one of my favorite saxophone players is that right?

Who’s that, oh Cannonball. Yeah. Oh yeah. After I won that talent contest I was in the sixth grade. I was just trying to get a baseball glove man. And I walked by this theater, it said $15 first prize, and the glove cost $13. So I went in and played my little boogie- woogie and I won the contest. But then they had eight weeks of that and all the winners competed for the big grand prize and I won that too. And so when I went back to school they made me the president of the class and all the girls would look at me.…

Adderley. And I’m blown away, what is this man? So I told my dad, you should hear what I heard. Because Cannonball gave me his card. So my dad had a street dance. So he said, “Hire him for the gig.” There had never been a mixed band in Fort Lauderdale. We were the first mixed band. And so I remember, because Cannonball, he must have been making about 70 dollars a week as a school teacher at Dillard High School. And that gig pays 75.
